label: 0038 · Smoothed in time, 1997–2025 (one QP over all windows of 0024): 0037 with block rotations estimated from the 1997–2011 record, correlated noise, fixed 747-site network, UNR positions (MAP)
description: 0037 with the block rotations estimated in the record model instead of fixed to the 2005–2011 reference solve, whose Hokkaido velocities carry the decade-long transient after the 2003 Tokachi-oki earthquake. The rotations of the 15 blocks with GEONET sites are static unknowns (prior SD 10 mm/yr at each block's sites, centred on the reference), estimated from the windows before Tohoku (1997–2011) and held fixed after it; the kinematic slip rates follow them. Estimated from every window instead, they took up the long post-Tohoku transient. Relative to the reference, the small blocks of central Honshu move 4–7 mm/yr east, the Hokkaido and northern Tohoku blocks 1–4 mm/yr, mostly east, and southwest Japan and the Ryukyus 2 mm/yr or less. The estimate does not move Hokkaido back toward its 1997–2003 velocities: the record's correlated noise (1.4 mm/yr over 150 km) treats an island-wide offset largely as noise, so the rotations are set mainly by shorter-wavelength velocity structure, and the model still runs about 7 mm/yr east of the 1997–2003 Hokkaido velocities. Window cross-validation is 357 above 0037's and higher in every window, including the post-Tohoku windows the rotations were not fit to (+234). Plain residuals are slightly larger before 2011 and smaller after. Background coupling rises by about 0.04 off Sanriku and 0.08 off Miyagi–Fukushima; Tohoku afterslip is unchanged. MAP solution, no posterior SD.
